title: If the singular ideal generates the unit ideal of Lambda, A -> Lambda factors through a smooth algebra
statement: Let $R\to A\to\Lambda$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation ($A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$), and let $H_{A/R}\subset A$ be the singular ideal of $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. If $H_{A/R}\Lambda=\Lambda$ (the ideal of $\Lambda$ generated by the image of $H_{A/R}$ is the unit ideal), then there are a smooth $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $A\to B\to\Lambda$ whose composite is the given map $A\to\Lambda$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve), Section 07C4; the proof there takes B = A[x_1,...,x_r]/(f_1x_1+...+f_rx_r-1) for f_i in H_{A/R}, lambda_i in Lambda with sum f_i lambda_i = 1, and leaves the smoothness check ('Details omitted')

proof.text: (Choice of $f_i,\lambda_i$.) Write $\varphi:A\to\Lambda$ for the given map. $H_{A/R}\Lambda$ is the set of finite sums $\sum_k\mu_k\varphi(h_k)$ with $h_k\in H_{A/R}$, $\mu_k\in\Lambda$; since it equals $\Lambda$ it contains $1$, so there are $r\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_r\in H_{A/R}$ and $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_r\in\Lambda$ with $\sum_{i=1}^r\varphi(f_i)\lambda_i=1$ in $\Lambda$. ($r=0$ is allowed; it happens only when $\Lambda=0$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve), first sentence

proof.text: (Construction of $B$ and the factorization.) Put $h=f_1x_1+\dots+f_rx_r-1\in A[x_1,\dots,x_r]$ and $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_r]/(h)$, an $R$-algebra via $R\to A\to B$. The $A$-algebra map $A[x_1,\dots,x_r]\to\Lambda$ (with $A$ acting through $\varphi$) sending $x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$ exists by the universal property of the polynomial ring and sends $h$ to $\sum\varphi(f_i)\lambda_i-1=0$ by step 1, so it factors through a ring map $\beta:B\to\Lambda$, $\bar x_i\mapsto\lambda_i$. By construction $\beta$ restricted to $A$ is $\varphi$, i.e. the composite $A\to B\xrightarrow{\beta}\Lambda$ is the given map; both maps are $A$-algebra maps, hence $R$-algebra maps. It remains to show that $B$ is smooth over $R$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve), second and third sentences

proof.text: ($A_{f_i}$ is smooth over $R$.) For each $i$, $f_i\in H_{A/R}$, so $A_{f_i}$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]. (Stacks says 'by definition of $H_{A/R}$'; with $H_{A/R}=\sqrt{(G)}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] this needs the cited lemma, since $f_i$ need not lie in $G$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve): 'A_{f_i} is smooth over R by definition of H_{A/R}'

proof.text: ($B_{f_i}$ is smooth over $A_{f_i}$.) Let $r\ge1$ and fix $i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-linear-equation-localization-polynomial], $B_{f_i}$ (localization of $B$ at the powers of the image of $f_i$) is isomorphic as an $A_{f_i}$-algebra, via the map $A_{f_i}\to B_{f_i}$ induced by $A\to B$, to the polynomial ring $A_{f_i}[y_j:j\ne i]$ in $r-1$ variables, which is smooth over $A_{f_i}$ [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth]. Smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is a property of the $A_{f_i}$-algebra up to isomorphism (an $A_{f_i}$-algebra isomorphism carries a finite presentation to a finite presentation and induces isomorphisms of naive cotangent complexes and of modules of differentials), so $A_{f_i}\to B_{f_i}$ is smooth.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve): 'and that B_{f_i} is smooth over A_{f_i}. Details omitted.'

proof.text: ($B_{f_i}$ is smooth over $R$.) The square $A\to A_{f_i}\to B_{f_i}$, $A\to B\to B_{f_i}$ commutes (both send $a\mapsto a/1$), so the $R$-algebra structure of $B_{f_i}$ through $R\to A\to B\to B_{f_i}$ equals the composite $R\to A_{f_i}\to B_{f_i}$. This is a composite of smooth ring maps (steps 3 and 4), hence smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (2).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07EU (lemma-final-solve): 'To check that B is smooth over R use that A_{f_i} is smooth over R ... and that B_{f_i} is smooth over A_{f_i}'

proof.text: In the explicit quotient B, the defining relation gives $\sum_i\bar f_i\bar x_i=1$, so the images of the f_i span the unit ideal. The polynomial ring in finitely many variables over the finitely presented R-algebra A is finitely presented, and its quotient by the principal relation is finitely presented (Mathlib Algebra.FinitePresentation.mvPolynomial and Algebra.FinitePresentation.quotient). Each localization is smooth by steps 3-5. Apply Algebra.basicOpen_subset_smoothLocus_iff_smooth to put each basic open in the smooth locus; PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff' makes these opens cover Spec(B). Thus the smooth locus is all of Spec(B), and Algebra.smoothLocus_eq_univ_iff gives formal smoothness. Together with finite presentation this proves smoothness, implementing [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-local-on-cover] in arbitrary universes. The same finite-sum and cover arguments include r=0 and the zero ring. Combine with the constructed maps to obtain the required factorization.
